title: Integral realization of saturated toric towers is proper after arbitrary base change
statement:
Let $P$ be a fine saturated additive commutative monoid with torsion-free group completion $G$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Let $M_0=\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}P$ and let $M_r\to\cdots\to M_0$ be a finite tower of saturated monoscheme blowups along coherent monoid ideals nonempty on every component [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. For a monoid $Q$, the ring $\mathbf Z[Q]$ has basis $z^q$ with $z^qz^{q'}=z^{q+q'}$. Define $\mathbf Z[M_i]$ by gluing these affine spectra along the monomial localization maps of the monoscheme charts. Let $A$ be any commutative ring with a homomorphism $\alpha:P\to(A,\cdot)$, and define
$$X_i=\operatorname{Spec}A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[M_i]$$
using the scheme fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then every $X_i\to X_{i-1}$, and their composite $\pi:X_r\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Each $M_i$ has a finite affine cover by monoids $Q\subseteq G$ containing $P$ with $Q^{\rm gp}=G$; the corresponding cover of $X_i$ has coordinate rings
$$A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q]$$
[def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with their specified monomial overlap maps. Refining a chart by a monoid localization gives the corresponding open localization of this ring. If $S=\{\alpha(p):p\in P\}$, every $X_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ restricts to an isomorphism over $\operatorname{Spec}S^{-1}A$; the localization consists of fractions with denominators in $S$. These assertions hold without flatness, log regularity or reducedness assumptions on $A$, and allow an empty base change and a length-zero tower.

source.place: VIII 3.2.9 and 3.2.17--3.2.18, printed pp.104--105 (toric saturation finite over the ordinary blowup); 3.3.5--3.3.11, printed pp.107--108 (chart base change). Integral-coefficient tower/base-change formulation supplied by O1; unlike the field-only existing toric comparison, the base of realization is Spec Z.

proof.text: Induct on the stage to obtain the asserted finite monoid-chart covers. At stage zero the chart is $P$. Suppose a chart at stage $i-1$ is $Q\subseteq G$, containing $P$, with $Q^{\rm gp}=G$, fine and saturated. The coherent center on this chart has a finite nonempty generating set $E\subset Q$. Indeed an affine monoid spectrum has a unique closed point (the ideal of nonunits); its only open neighbourhood is the entire spectrum, so the local finite generation in the definition gives such $E$. For $a\in E$ put $C_a=\langle Q,b-a\ (b\in E)\rangle\subseteq G$. This is finitely generated, integral, contains $P$, and has group completion $G$ because it contains $Q$. By [lem-trf-fine-monoid-finite-saturation], $C_a^{\rm sat}$ is fine saturated with the same group completion and saturation commutes with localization. The prescribed saturated-blowup charts and overlaps in [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization, def-trf-fine-fan-blowup] are precisely these monoids and their common localizations. Finitely many old charts and finitely many generators on each give finitely many new charts. This proves the inductive claim for every stage.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17--3.1.21, printed p.101; finite chart induction expanded

proof.text: Fix one chart $Q$ and center $E$ from Step 1, put $R=\mathbf Z[Q]$ and $J=(z^b:b\in E)\subset R$, and write $B=\operatorname{Bl}_J(\operatorname{Spec}R)$. Its $a$-chart is $\operatorname{Spec}R[J/z^a]$ by [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover, def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. The localization $R_{z^a}$ embeds in $\mathbf Z[G]$: translating exponents by $-na$ takes distinct basis exponents to distinct exponents, so a fraction can map to zero only if its numerator is zero. Inside this ring the subalgebra generated by $R$ and $z^b/z^a$ is exactly $\mathbf Z[C_a]$: products of its generators have exponents in $C_a$, and every exponent in $C_a$ is a sum of such exponents. Thus the chart identification sends $z^{q+\sum_j(b_j-a)}$ to $z^q\prod_j(z^{b_j}/z^a)$. It is an isomorphism over $R$, obtained directly over the integers; a field-only normalization result is unnecessary. These are identities of subalgebras, including all additive relations, rather than a presentation obtained by treating monomial ratios as algebraically independent.

source.place: VIII proof of Lemma 3.2.17, printed p.105, with its monomial-basis chart calculation over Z; Stacks divisors.tex Tag 0804, lemma-blowing-up-affine

proof.text: The identifications in Step 2 have exactly the prescribed transition maps. Under the chart map of [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart, def-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-map], the degree-zero fraction $(z^bt)/(z^at)$ is $z^{b-a}$ by [def-nagata-homogeneous-away-to-chart]. The intersection of the two standard opens is $D_+(z^at)\cap D_+(z^bt)$ [lem-weil-pbc-proj-standard-open-inclusion], hence in the $a$-chart it is $D(z^{b-a})$; in the $b$-chart it is $D(z^{a-b})$. Both localized rings are the same subring $\mathbf Z[C_a+\mathbf N(a-b)]=\mathbf Z[C_b+\mathbf N(b-a)]$ of $\mathbf Z[G]$, and the transition is the identity on monomials. The elementary equality follows because inverting $b-a$ makes $a-b$ available and $c-b=(c-a)+(a-b)$. The same formulas remain identities after replacing $Q$ by any monoid localization and extending the center. Consequently the realization of the unsaturated blowup over this chart is $B$, with its actual overlap maps. Since $J$ is generated by the finite set $z^E$, $B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-affine-blowup-proper]. The identification of a principal open with the spectrum of its principal localization is [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](b).

source.place: VIII proof of 3.2.17, printed p.105; Stacks divisors.tex Tag 0804, lemma-blowing-up-affine, and Tag 02NS, lemma-blowing-up-projective

proof.text: Let $V_a=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[C_a^{\rm sat}]$ and $U_a=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[C_a]\subset B$. The inclusions of monoids give maps $V_a\to U_a$. By [lem-trf-fine-monoid-finite-saturation], saturation commutes with the localizations in Step 3, so these maps glue to $s:V\to B$, where $V$ is the specified saturated-blowup realization above $\operatorname{Spec}R$. Its full inverse image of $U_a$ is $V_a$, not merely an open containing $V_a$: on $V_b$ the inverse image of $U_a\cap U_b$ is $D(z^{a-b})$, and its localized ring is the common saturated overlap, already identified with the corresponding open $D(z^{b-a})$ of $V_a$. Taking the union over $b$ proves $s^{-1}U_a=V_a$. The same cited saturation lemma, with coefficient ring $\mathbf Z$, says that $\mathbf Z[C_a^{\rm sat}]$ is a finite $\mathbf Z[C_a]$-module. Thus each $V_a\to U_a$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-finite-ring-map-finite], and $s$ is finite by the affine-cover criterion [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-on-target]. The identification of a principal open with the spectrum of its principal localization is [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](b).

source.place: VIII proof of 3.2.9, printed p.104 (finite saturation); Stacks morphisms.tex Tag 01WI, lemma-finite-local

proof.text: For the chart in Steps 2--4, $s$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]; composing it with the proper blowup $B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. Restricting a monoscheme blowup to an old affine chart is the same chart construction with its restricted center, by the localization prescription of [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. The realization of that restriction is the full inverse image of the realized affine chart: on monomial basic opens this is exactly inversion of the same monomials, and these opens are the gluings defining both realizations. Therefore these proper local maps are the restrictions of $\mathbf Z[M_i]\to\mathbf Z[M_{i-1}]$ to an affine open cover of its target. Properness local on the target [lemma-nagata-projective-target-local] proves that every integral-realization transition is proper. Composing finitely many transitions again gives a proper morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]$.

source.place: VIII 3.2.9, 3.2.17--3.2.18, printed pp.104--105; properness assembled locally from finite saturation and ordinary blowups

proof.text:
Pull the finite chart cover of Step 1 back along $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] these pullbacks are open subschemes covering $X_i$, and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] gives their rings $B_Q=A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q]$, with structural maps $a\mapsto a\otimes1$ and $z^q\mapsto1\otimes z^q$. For any submonoid $T\subseteq Q$, localization is explicitly
$$B_Q[(1\otimes z^t)^{-1}:t\in T]\ \simeq\ A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q-T],\qquad (a\otimes z^q)/(1\otimes z^t)\longmapsto a\otimes z^{q-t}.$$
The inverse sends $a\otimes z^{q-t}$ to that fraction; the monoid and tensor relations are preserved, and the localization universal property [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property] makes the two maps inverse on all generators. This also proves that the chart overlap maps are exactly the specified monomial maps after tensoring. The localization is open: choose finite monoid generators of $Q$. Inverting $T$ is equivalent to inverting the finitely many generators occurring in expressions for elements of $T$ (a product is a unit exactly when each factor is); it is the principal localization at their product. No injectivity of $B_Q$ into a fraction ring is used. The identification of a principal open with the spectrum of its principal localization is [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](b).

source.place: VIII 3.3.5--3.3.6, printed p.107; Stacks schemes.tex Tags 01I4/01JQ, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes/lemma-fibre-product-affines, and 01JR, lemma-open-fibre-product; algebra.tex Tag 00CP, proposition-universal-property-localization

proof.text: The square with top arrow $X_i\to X_{i-1}$ and bottom arrow $\mathbf Z[M_i]\to\mathbf Z[M_{i-1}]$ is Cartesian. In fact, giving a morphism into $X_{i-1}\times_{\mathbf Z[M_{i-1}]}\mathbf Z[M_i]$ is, by [def-pc-fibre-product], exactly giving compatible morphisms into $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\mathbf Z[M_i]$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]$, which is the defining universal property of $X_i$. Each $X_i\to X_{i-1}$ is therefore proper by Step 5 and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], and their composite is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. At length zero $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and the composite is its identity. This is proper directly from [def-weil-proper-morphism]: its diagonal and all its base changes are identities and it is of finite type. These arguments apply to arbitrary $A$ and also to the zero ring.

source.place: VIII 3.3.5, printed p.107 (ordinary scheme chart base change); properness by arbitrary base change and composition

proof.text: Finally put $L=S^{-1}A$, $S=\alpha(P)$. In the integral model, inverting all monomials of $P$ changes every chart monoid $Q$ to $Q-P=G$: $P\subseteq Q\subseteq G=P^{\rm gp}$, and every element of $G$ is $p-p'$ with $p,p'\in P$. The formulas of Step 6 and [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property] identify the base change of $B_Q$ to $L$ with $L$. Explicitly the inverse to $L\to L\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q]$ sends $l\otimes z^q$ to $l\alpha(p)\alpha(p')^{-1}$ for $q=p-p'$. The value is independent of that expression since for two expressions $p_1-p_2=p_3-p_4$ equality of differences gives $p_1+p_4=p_3+p_2$ in the integral monoid $P$, and applying $\alpha$ and inverting $S$ gives the same fraction. Inductively all old charts share this same group-algebra locus, and each new center chart contains it. All overlap monomials become units, so every pulled-back overlap is all of $\operatorname{Spec}L$, and the transition maps are identities under these identifications. The charts consequently glue to one copy of $\operatorname{Spec}L$, and all tower maps are its identity. Fractions in $L$ have exactly denominators from $S$. If some element of $S$ is zero or nilpotent, $L=0$ and these are identities of empty schemes; no nonemptiness, flatness, reducedness or log regularity assumption was introduced.

Read ILO VIII 3.2.8-3.2.9, 3.2.14-3.2.18 and 3.3.5-3.3.8 in the local PDF. The proof is the chart comparison of 3.2.17, done over Z instead of a field, plus the finiteness sentence of 3.2.9 and the chart base change of 3.3.5. Shape: one commit; the statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint are identical to live; live still has the item unsplit, so no parallel group superseded it; no repair note; no SGA. Step 1: the induction is set up. The closed point of Spec_mon Q has no smaller open neighbourhood, so the centre has a finite nonempty generating set E. C_a=<Q,b-a> has group completion G, and the finite-saturation lemma gives C_a^sat. Step 2: Z[Q]_{z^a} embeds in Z[G], and the chart ring equals Z[C_a]. Marking it elementary is justified. Step 3: theta_a gives z^{b-a}, and clause (0) of the Proj standard-open lemma gives the overlap D(z^{b-a}). I checked C_a+N(a-b)=C_b+N(b-a). The blowup is proper because J is finitely generated. Step 4: saturation commutes with localization, s^{-1}U_a=V_a on every V_b, and the saturated chart ring is a finite module over Z. Criterion (2) of finite-local-on-target then gives finiteness. Step 5: finite implies proper, composites are proper, and properness is local on the target, using the chart-restriction prescription of the definition. Step 6: localization commutes with the tensor product, the inverse is well defined, and inverting any T reduces to inverting finitely many generators. Step 7: pasting of pullbacks and base change along an arbitrary map; length zero is the identity. Step 8: Q-P=G, the base change to S^{-1}A is S^{-1}A on every chart, and the overlaps are everything. Edge cases tested: r=0, a single generator, N^2 with both charts, a non-saturated <2,3>, A=0, L=0 through a zero or nilpotent alpha(p), and a nonflat A. Duplicates checked: lem-trf-toric-blowup-chart-normalization is over a field only; lem-trf-log-ideal-saturation-chart-finiteness needs log chart data and only covers Step 4; lem-trf-toric-chart-fs-realization and three other lem-trf toric-tower nodes do not state properness of the integral realization. Batch 5: def-trf-fine-fan-blowup is a general definition, and lem-trf-fine-monoid-finite-saturation is generic monoid algebra whose closure is Gordan and cone lemmas. Neither is given by or part of the proof of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so both are accepted. Tool uses accepted: fine-monoid-finite-saturation, and clause (0) of lem-weil-pbc-proj-standard-open-inclusion. No changes made.
